180f2b497d1bc1c7.what: First-principles plus Boltzmann transport study of monolayer and Ab-stacked bilayer R-graphyne. Lattice κ at 300 K is 150.97 (monolayer) and 50.60 W/m/K (bilayer); max n-type ZT is 0.889 (monolayer, 700 K) and 1.943 (bilayer, 300 K).
180f2b497d1bc1c7.why: Understand how Ab stacking changes the balance of electronic and phonon transport.
180f2b497d1bc1c7.how: HSE06 electronic structure with Boltzmann transport under deformation-potential and relaxation-time approximations; the bilayer shows shorter phonon lifetimes.
180f2b497d1bc1c7.impact: Low relevance: a standard DFT+BTE workflow on a 2D carbon material with no direct link to the GaN, InGaAs or BAs projects.

a01c5e057ae23f69.what: Electrothermal comparison of GaN (GS66508B), SiC and Si MOSFETs in a 3 kW, 400 V/200 V buck converter at 50–200 kHz. Losses at 100 kHz are 7.5126, 19.6845 and 47.8417 W (GaN, SiC, Si); efficiencies 99.75%, 99.34%, 98.39%.
a01c5e057ae23f69.why: Assess power loss and junction temperature of wide-bandgap devices for EV charging.
a01c5e057ae23f69.how: LTspice loss simulation (conduction loss plus integrated switching energy) feeding a Cauer RC thermal network (junction-case, case-heatsink, heatsink-ambient) for transient junction temperature.
a01c5e057ae23f69.impact: Circuit-level compact thermal modelling; useful context for the GaN/AlGaN HEMT self-heating project (what device-scale models feed into) and electronics thermal-management trends, but no atomistic or BTE content.

7b330599b5ea0b74.what: First-principles study of full Heusler K2XSi (X = Ca, Mg) for optical and thermoelectric performance (from the title).
7b330599b5ea0b74.how: First-principles calculations per the title. Not stated in the abstract.
7b330599b5ea0b74.impact: Low relevance: no abstract available and a routine thermoelectric DFT screening; no link to the listed projects.

d717c7e3272fe1b1.what: DFT, Boltzmann transport and CGCNN study of Ti/Mn/Ni-decorated hydrogen-passivated armchair stanene nanoribbons for gas sensing; adsorption strength on Mn-ASnNR follows SO2 > NO2 > NH3.
d717c7e3272fe1b1.why: Evaluate transition-metal-decorated nanoribbons as toxic-gas sensors.
d717c7e3272fe1b1.how: DFT adsorption calculations, Boltzmann transport, and CGCNN predictions of thermomechanical parameters.
d717c7e3272fe1b1.impact: Low relevance: gas-sensing application; the only transferable point is the use of a graph neural network for property prediction.

aa5baa95bee72a02.what: DFT study of La2CdS4 and La2MgS4: both stable and ductile (B/G > 1.75) with positive Seebeck coefficients; La2MgS4 has higher thermopower, lower κe and better ZT.
aa5baa95bee72a02.why: Compare how Mg versus Cd substitution affects stability, optical and thermoelectric behaviour.
aa5baa95bee72a02.how: DFT for electronic, optical, elastic and thermoelectric properties. Transport model details are not stated in the abstract.
aa5baa95bee72a02.impact: Low relevance: routine DFT property survey; lattice thermal conductivity and phonons are not mentioned.

1184aedde8332137.what: Open-source browser-based LAMMPS tool: input-script builder, MD notebook with an engine checked against native LAMMPS, CMake helper and GPU 3D viewer for LAMMPS data/dump, XYZ, PDB and CIF.
1184aedde8332137.why: Let users run and visualise MD with no install and nothing uploaded.
1184aedde8332137.impact: Low-moderate: handy for quick LAMMPS input prototyping or teaching, but not a replacement for DeePMD/MACE thermal-MD runs on HPC.

13e7d444a150a559.what: lab-cosmo's atomistic-cookbook: a collection of simulation recipes for atomic-scale modeling of materials and molecules.
13e7d444a150a559.why: Share reproducible worked examples for atomistic ML and simulation.
13e7d444a150a559.how: Python repository of recipes; details are not stated in the abstract.
13e7d444a150a559.impact: Moderate: from a leading MLIP group, so it may hold example workflows relevant to the MLPhonon and MACE pipelines; worth a skim.

a7e1cea41977ab76.what: horus-runtime: open-source runtime to run reproducible scientific workflows on a laptop, remote machine or HPC (Slurm) from a single YAML file.
a7e1cea41977ab76.why: Make workflows portable and reproducible across environments.
a7e1cea41977ab76.how: Python CLI with DAG-based pipelines defined in YAML.
a7e1cea41977ab76.impact: Low-moderate: possibly useful for chaining VASP/phono3py/LAMMPS steps on HPC, but the abstract shows no agent or first-principles features.

9ec26cd6116f55b2.what: Packmol.jl: Julia implementation of packing optimization for building initial MD configurations.
9ec26cd6116f55b2.why: Generate non-overlapping starting structures for MD.
9ec26cd6116f55b2.how: Julia package; topics mention LAMMPS, GROMACS and NAMD.
9ec26cd6116f55b2.impact: Low relevance: aimed at molecular systems; the crystalline semiconductor and interface models in the projects do not need packing.

153aeb3a23443ba7.what: NQCDynamics.jl: Julia package for nonadiabatic, quantum-classical and semi-classical molecular dynamics.
153aeb3a23443ba7.how: Julia code with MD and Monte Carlo methods.
153aeb3a23443ba7.impact: Low relevance: nonadiabatic dynamics is outside the phonon-transport projects.

c0569d254f7567f3.what: seams-core: C++ core engine of d-SEAMS for MD trajectory analysis (ice, clathrate hydrates, topology).
c0569d254f7567f3.how: C++20 with Lua scripting, nauty and PLUMED.
c0569d254f7567f3.impact: Low relevance: aimed at water/ice structure analysis, not phonons or semiconductors.

fc69ec86f4d18072.what: AI4Mat workshop at NeurIPS 2026 website updated: AI for accelerated materials design, December 12, 2026, Sydney, Australia.
fc69ec86f4d18072.why: Bring AI researchers and materials scientists together on AI-driven materials discovery.
fc69ec86f4d18072.how: Short workshop papers; no deadline sentences found on the page.
fc69ec86f4d18072.impact: Topic fits MLIP interpretability and agent work, but it is held in Sydney (not US) and is imminent, so it is not a practical submission target; watch for a 2027 edition.

new_items.title: AI for Computational Physical Science (APL Computational Physics Special Topic)
new_items.abstract: AI methods for theoretical and computational physical science, focusing on condensed matter, materials, chemical physics, molecular systems and quantum simulations. Welcomes new algorithms, AI-accelerated simulation, ML combined with physical constraints, interpretability, and reproducible datasets, benchmarks and open-source software. Topics include machine-learning interatomic potentials, AI-accelerated electronic-structure methods, active learning, multiscale modeling and interpretable AI. Guest editors: Hongjun Xiang, Jian Sun, Fang Liu.

summary.what: Special topic in APL Computational Physics on AI for computational physical science, including MLIPs, active learning and multiscale modeling.
summary.why: Collect new AI methods, benchmarks and open-source software for condensed-matter and materials simulation.
summary.how: Submit through the journal's portal by 2027-01-31 (the page lists the deadline and a contribute link; confirm status in the portal).
summary.impact: Good fit for the MLPhonon workflow, the InGaAs DeepPotential-vs-MACE comparison or active-learning BAs MLIPs; worth considering for a submission.
